source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: While those bears, monkeys, and Rakshasas were thus dwelling, the greatly effulgent Rama then spoke these words to Sugriva.
verses.2: O gentle one, go to Kishkindha, which is unassailable even by gods and demons, and rule your kingdom with your ministers, having removed all its enemies.
verses.3: O mighty-armed one, you should look upon Angada, Hanuman, and Nala of great strength with supreme affection.
verses.4: Also see the brave Sushena, your father-in-law, Tara, the best among the strong, and the unassailable Kumuda, and Nila of great strength.
verses.5: Look with affection upon the brave Shatavali, Mainda, Dvivida, Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya, Sharabha of great strength, and Gandhamadana.
verses.6: Also see Rishabha, the very valorous, and Jambavan of great strength, and all these other great-souled beings who risked their lives for my sake.
verses.7: You should look upon them with affection and never cause them any harm.
verses.8: Having spoken thus and repeatedly embraced Sugriva, Rama then addressed Vibhishana with sweet words.
verses.9: Rule Lanka righteously, for I consider you knowledgeable in dharma, and you are indeed approved by your own brother, by the city, and by the Rakshasas.
verses.10: O King, never let your mind incline towards unrighteousness, for intelligent kings certainly rule the earth.
verses.11: O King, you should always remember me and Sugriva with great affection; now go, free from all sorrow.
verses.12: Having heard Rama's words, the bears, monkeys, and rakshasas repeatedly praised him, exclaiming "Excellent! Excellent!"
verses.13: O mighty-armed Rama, your intellect and valor are truly wonderful, and your supreme sweetness is eternal, like that of the Self-born Brahma.
verses.14: While the monkeys and rakshasas were speaking thus, Hanuman, bowing down humbly, addressed Rama.
verses.15: O King, may my supreme affection for you remain always, and O hero, may my devotion be unwavering, with my feelings never straying elsewhere.
verses.16: O hero, as long as the story of Rama is told on the earth, my life breaths will undoubtedly remain in my body.
verses.17: O Rama, delight of the Raghus and best among men, may the Apsaras indeed make me hear this divine story and your divine deeds.
verses.18: O hero, O lord, having heard that nectar-like story of your deeds, I shall then remove that longing/sorrow, just as the wind disperses a line of clouds.
verses.19: Rama, having risen from his excellent seat, embraced Hanuman who was speaking thus, and out of affection, indeed spoke these words.
verses.20: O best of monkeys, it will indeed be so, there is no doubt about it; as long as this story of mine spreads in the world, so long will your fame and life-breaths remain in your body.
verses.21: Indeed, as long as the worlds exist, so long will my story endure.
verses.22: Rama declares that his gratitude is such that he would give his life for each of Hanuman's favors, emphasizing that a person becomes worthy of receiving return favors even when in distress.
verses.23: Then, Rama took off his own moon-like necklace from his neck and fastened it, adorned with a cat's eye gem, onto Hanuman's neck.
verses.24: With that great necklace fastened on his chest, Hanuman shone like a magnificent golden mountain whose peak is adorned by the moon.
verses.25: Having heard these words from Rama, those mighty monkeys repeatedly rose, bowed their heads at his feet, and then departed.
verses.26: Sugriva, who was constantly embraced by Rama, and the righteous Vibhishana, along with all the others, were overcome with tears.
verses.27: At that time, all of them, full of tears and with tearful eyes, were bewildered and stupefied by sorrow as they were leaving Rama.
verses.28: Having thus received grace from the great-souled Rama, all of them returned to their respective homes, feeling as if an embodied soul abandoning its body.
verses.29: Then, those Rakshasas, bears, and monkeys, having bowed down to Rama, the enhancer of the Raghu dynasty, returned to their respective abodes with eyes full of tears born of separation. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 40 ।। Thus ends the fortieth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
verses.30: Thus ends the fortieth canto of the Uttara Kanda in the Ramayana, the first poem, composed by the sage Valmiki.
